failure_summary: Board check (visualize_board.sh, after-best movestring 2345153551111014334) shows the better move (col5) lands at c5r3 and the game ends immediately ('[GAME OVER]', X wins outright completing c3r1/c4r2/c5r3/c6r4); the assembled prompt explicitly states this as a completed fact ('wins on the spot ... the game is over there') and explicitly instructs 'never future tense ("threat to make four next move", "keep it for the next turn") for a move that already ended the game' — yet both runs frame the better move with exactly that banned future-tense/ongoing-threat pattern ('preserved your next-move four and forced them to answer it' / 'You had to keep the next-move four-in-a-row threat ... alive'), matching the rubric's explicit A7a fail example 'the better move keeps the win alive' instead of stating the decisive fact that the move wins outright — production-fidelity run (model=gpt-5.4-mini, same as production), so this cannot be fully separated from model capability; a contributing render-layer issue is noted below.
notes: Both runs fail A7a: they narrate the better move (col5, completing the four at c5r3) as merely 'keeping a threat alive' / something that must still 'force' a reply, when visualize_board.sh confirms the move ends the game immediately (X wins outright) — the same result-restating pattern the rubric explicitly calls out ('the better move keeps the win alive'). A1/A2/A6 pass per grade_mechanical.mjs (eval-41|D|0 and |1: A1 pass, A2 pass, A6 pass, G7a_offered pass, G7b_offered pass). A3/A4 checked against the board (decision board: visualize_board.sh 234515355111101433 shows major threat col5 row3 (X) [GT]; after-best board 2345153551111014334 shows '[GAME OVER]' with the c3r1/c4r2/c5r3/c6r4 diagonal complete; after-played+occupation board 23451535511110143364 shows O occupying c5r3, all X column scores negative afterward) — the named mechanism (immediate_threat denied by occupation) is real and decisive, so A3/A4 pass despite the A7a framing defect. A5 passes both runs (2nd person, no banned internal/vector terminology; A5b n/a — player 1). G1-G6 pass (link.guardrail honored: correct move attributed to player, not opponent; boards/finalMovestring/threat-list all board-true per visualize_board.sh). G7 pass both runs: zone handles you-immediate/you-immediate-line and term immediate_threat are all offered (render_decision.zones) and wrap phrases matching their stated role; annotationRepairs is empty on both rows so no G7c auto-fail. Sub-sampling n/a — only 2 runs total exist for this case (not the assumed 5), so both were graded on every axis.

counterexamples.evidence: assembleGroundedPrompt(buildReasonRenderModel(feature_vector)) includes the reading-key instruction 'When the better move wins outright, the frame says so as a completed, present fact ("wins on the spot", "the game is over there") — never future tense ("threat to make four next move", "keep it for the next turn") for a move that already ended the game.' Yet the SAME assembled prompt offers a term (immediate_threat) whose own canonicalPhrase is literally 'threat to make four next move' — the exact banned phrase — for this record, where completingCell (c5r3) IS bestCol and playing it ends the game (verified: visualize_board.sh 2345153551111014334 shows '[GAME OVER]'). Run 1's mechanism used this term almost verbatim ('the next-move four-in-a-row threat'). This is a render-layer inconsistency (render_bug): the offered term's own definition contradicts the reading-key rule for a case where the tag's completing cell coincides with the outright-winning move; it should not be offered with 'next move' wording (or a different, register-aware term should be offered) when the immediate_threat's completingCell equals bestCol and the position is a forced/immediate win.

counterexamples.field_or_glossary: render_decision.link.text prose vs. model's own free text
counterexamples.evidence: render_decision.link.text correctly reads 'The better move (col 5) completes your threat to make four next move at c5r3; the played move let the opponent take c5r3, denying it' (also legacy 'next move' wording, but PROMPT.includes shows the ACTUAL assembled prompt replaces this with 'it wins on the spot ... the game is over there' — confirmed via renderReasonModel.mjs's assembleGroundedPrompt output). Run 0's phrase 'preserved your next-move four and forced them to answer it' is NOT present anywhere in the assembled prompt (PROMPT does not contain 'forced them to answer') and directly contradicts the prompt's own explicit instruction against future-tense framing for an outright win — the model introduced this framing itself despite an unambiguous, correctly-stated instruction in the same prompt, which is prompt_confusion, not a render/vector gap.
